newsitem.title: SWEDEN: S-E-Banken says to open Denmark office.
newsitem.headline: S-E-Banken says to open Denmark office.

text.p: Swedish commercial bank S-E-Banken said on Tuesday it would open a branch in Denmark in the first half of 1997.

"During the first half of 1997 Skandinaviska Enskilda Banken intends to establish a branch in Denmark, where it is already active through its credit and charge card company Diners Club," S-E-Banken said in a statement.
The bank said it would increase its Danish activities to include a broader range of banking services, mostly in the corporate sector.
It said this was part of its strategy to reach a leading position in the Nordic region. S-E-Banken has had branches in Oslo and Helsinki for a couple of years.
The proposal is subject to approval by Sweden's Financial Supervisory Authority, the bank said.
